transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~90 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (PM), Evan Liu (Eng Manager), Maya Gomez (SRE), Noah Patel (Release Lead), Alex Rivera (VP Product), Samir Khan (Head of Infra), Dana Ortiz (Legal) and a few engineers (on quiet).

Summary (auto): Roadmap and launch readiness for Q4. Main decision points: agree on hard launch criteria (latency and error budget), finalize launch freeze and rollback policy, complete SOC2 checklist items, run a DR/incident simulation pre-launch.

00:00 Priya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh we have a lot to cover. goal is to lock the launch checklist, call out owners, and make sure the incident follow-up from last week is closed.
01:02 Evan: yeah quick note — the perf bench this morning showed a small regen in p50 when using the new kernel set, about +8%. we need to understand if that's infra or model-side.
02:10 Maya: s o we ran the KV cache change in staging, and there was a spike in tail latency around 95th. seemed related to cold cache on certain shards. we have debug logs but it's not fully root-caused.
03:30 Alex: right so for launch we need to be conservative, we can't have that kind of tail behavior. what's the mitigation?
03:50 Evan: short term we can enforce pre-warm and a rolling warm-up job; long term, compilers/kernels need a small patch. also batching config impacts it.
05:20 Priya: action: Evan to deliver a perf test plan and suggested batching knobs by next Tuesday.
06:00 Noah: on release process — we need to pick the exact freeze window. sales asks for earlier GA but infra needs a solid 2-week buffer.
07:15 Priya: propose freeze start 2026-03-20 and final go/no-go 2026-03-31. does that align?
07:40 Samir: that gives infra one week to ramp after freeze; okay but only if we hit the perf gates.
08:55 Dana: legal/compliance — SOC2 evidence collection still has a few outstanding items, specifically around key management and audit log retention. we need to confirm KMS rotation policies and HSM access docs.
10:12 Maya: we have KMS integration; however the documentation needs updates. I'll own putting that in the SOC2 folder.
11:05 Priya: Dana will validate. Dana?
11:15 Dana: yes I'll review and flag gaps.
12:00 Evan: quick aside — for private deployments / VPC customers we still have the autoscaling change to surface in the console. that needs docs.
13:20 Priya: noted, add docs.
14:00 Transcript note: minor audio glitch, speaker overlap.
15:00 Priya: next topic, incident review from 2026-02-26 outage — Maya can you run through the timeline?
15:22 Maya: sure. at ~14:05 UTC we saw a spike in error rates driven by a canary that misrouted KV cache keys after a config push. autoscaler scaled down because of mistaken CPU metrics; downstream requests hit cold caches and latency spiked. there was a brief rollback but the rollback didn't flush some stale config.
17:10 Evan: right and the canary config was pushed without a gated rollout, team assumed default gating. that's on us.
18:00 Maya: mitigation steps we did — revert canary, manual scale up, and flush cache. post-mortem is in drive. root cause: no gating on the specific config type + metrics not instrumented for kv-warm states.
19:40 Priya: so for launch the requirement is gated rollouts for any kv or kernel-level config changes and a DR run.
20:15 Noah: DR run — we should schedule a full DR where we simulate a canary misconfig and exercise rollback. Maya can lead.
20:40 Maya: yes. I'll schedule DR and invite platform and on-call.
21:10 Priya: add that to action items.
22:00 Alex: product question — what's the perf target? p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5%?
22:30 Evan: those are reasonable but p95 350 is tight for some long-context; we might need to split based on model size or a graduated SLA: hosted GA vs dedicated.
23:50 Priya: agreed — define tiered SLAs. for GA (hosted) we'll set conservative targets and call out dedicated to support lower latency.
25:00 Samir: capacity plan — we need committed nodes for Dedicated customers and the Dedicated rollout must be separate from GA so we don't conflate capacity.
26:10 Priya: note — Dedicated launch will be phased, not day-one.
27:00 Dana: compliance note — need to ensure audit logs are immutable and that we can show retention policies. also confirm encryption at rest with KMS + HSM access patterns.
28:50 Maya: we already have encryption at rest; I'll gather evidence.
30:00 Priya: timing check — how close are we to having the performance benchmarks we trust? Evan?
30:30 Evan: baseline runs complete for small model. medium and large still in progress. hit an issue with kernel 2 patch which is causing the p50 regression mentioned earlier. local workaround exists but we need stable kernels.
32:20 Alex: can we postpone medium/large to a later gate if small works? customers care about larger models though.
33:00 Evan: not ideal but we can stage — GA supports small-medium; large is flagged and will require dedicated capacity as a recommendation.
34:30 Priya: decision: gate = small + medium validated; large will be separate and communicated.
35:45 Noah: release strategy — can we do canary rollout by customer segment? that reduces blast radius.
36:10 Maya: yes and must include warm-up preloads to avoid cold cache.
37:00 Evan: also add auto-fallback to a compatible model variant if quantization causes quality regressions.
38:45 Priya: quality checkpoints — link to eval suite must be green before final. Evan to run evals.
39:05 Evan: noted.
40:00 Transcript: brief cross-talk, sounds of typing.
41:15 Priya: risk register — let's list top 5: kernel perf regression, KV cold-cache tail, SOC2 evidence gaps, release coordination, and observability blind spots.
42:20 Maya: observability blind spots are real — we need better KV-warm state metrics and token-level tracing for a short window.
43:15 Evan: token-level tracing has privacy implications; only enable in limited debugging windows and scrub PII.
44:10 Dana: legal ok as long as we have documented retention and access controls.
45:00 Priya: owners assigned in action items.
46:20 Noah: timeline recap: freeze 3/20, go/no-go 3/31, DR run 3/10, perf sign-off 3/09, SOC2 evidence close 3/15.
47:30 Priya: confirm deliverables: final checklist, perf spreadsheets, DR run notes, compliance evidence, release communication.
48:00 Alex: can we draft a brief for sales/CS on limitations for GA so they don't oversell?
48:20 Priya: yes Noah, please prepare a short one-pager.
49:00 Noah: will do.
50:10 Maya: one more note — for on-prem/private we need to ensure our installer supports KMS rotations; there was an issue in 0.9.8.
51:00 Evan: we'll bump the package and test with the automation harness.
52:20 Priya: any blockers from legal? Dana?
52:40 Dana: nothing blocking but need two weeks to validate SOC2 packages. I'll prioritize.
54:00 Priya: ok moving to rollout specifics — canary sizes, metrics gating and fallback policies.
55:10 Evan: propose gating on p95, error rate and KV hit ratio. if p95 or error spikes, automatically stop rollout and escalate.
56:30 Maya: add a manual override to force rollback if metrics are flaky.
57:25 Priya: sounds good.
58:00 Transcript note: small audio drop for ~10s.
59:00 Alex: last strategic question — what are the go/no-go criteria that the execs will sign off on?
59:20 Priya: propose: 1) Perf gates met for small+medium; 2) Incident DR run completed w/ rollbacks verified; 3) SOC2 evidence 'in progress' with no critical gaps; 4) Release comms and freeze in place.
60:50 Alex: that seems reasonable. sign-off will be contingent on those.
62:00 Priya: wrap up — we'll circulate the checklist and owners. thanks everyone.
63:00 Maya: I'll attach post-mortem and DR playbook to the checklist.
64:00 Noah: I'll draft the freeze window notice and sales one-pager.
65:00 Dana: I'll run SOC2 review.
66:00 Evan: perf spreadsheets to be shared.
67:00 Priya: meeting adjourned.

Notes/Attachments referenced: link: drive/repo/roadmap/q4-launch-checklist (doc), link: drive/ops/perf-benchmarks.xlsx, link: drive/incidents/2026-02-26-postmortem (doc).

End transcript.
